Rotura compleja de la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco medial con leve extrusión meniscal.

normales .

Condropatía grado 4 difusa de la articulación patelofemoral.

5. Grade 3-4 chondromalacia and mild subchondral edema of femoral trochlea(Srs/Img: [ID].
6. Moderate joint effsuion and synovitis of right knee and patellar plicae.

ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ: - Στον έξω µηνίσκο παρατηρείται ρήξη «δίκην λαβής κάδου» (bucket handle) µε αναδίπλωση του τεµαχίου προς το πρόσθιο κέρας (flipped meniscus). Η ρήξη επεκτείνεται στην οπίσθια ρίζα, η οποία διατέµνεται πλήρως. ∆εν ελέγχεται υπεξάρθρηµα του σώµατος του. - Μικρός οστικός µώλωπας (bone bruise) ελέγχεται στον έξω µηριαίο κόνδυλο παρά την µεσοκονδύλια εντοµή. - Χόνδρινη κάκωση µερικού πάχους (grade II κατά ICRS) στην µεσότητα της επιγονατίδας, διαµέτρου 6mm, µε ανάδειξη µικρού πτερυγίου (flap), διαµέτρου 5mm. Συνυπάρχουν σχισµοειδείς διαβρώσεις στην έσω αρθρική επιφάνεια (fraying). - Ήπια τενοντοπάθεια του επιγονατιδικού τένοντα στην κνηµιαία πρόσφυση του. - Παρουσία ενδοστικού γαγγλίου στο οπίσθιο τµήµα του έξω κνηµιαίου κονδύλου, διαµέτρου 14mm. - Ευµεγέθης ενδαρθρική συλλογή υγρού. - Φυσιολογικά απεικονίζονται ο έσω µηνίσκος, οι χιαστοί και οι πλάγιοι σύνδεσµοι. - Με φυσιολογικό σήµα ελέγχεται ο λοιπός οστικός µυελός.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain and swelling
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. 5 mm intra-articular body posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. Small intraosseous ganglion in the tibia at the posterior meniscal root insertion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild chondrosis. Small marginal osteophytes in the medial joint compartment.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild chondrosis. Small marginal osteophytes in the lateral joint compartment.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Severe loss of cartilage along the lateral patellar facet and lateral femoral trochlea with marginal osteophyte formation and small foci of subchondral marrow edema. There is full thickness cartilage fissuring in the central femoral trochlea and a small full thickness cartilage defect along the medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Tricompartmental knee osteoarthritis, greatest in the patellofemoral joint compartment.
2. Small knee joint effusion.
3. No meniscal tear.

TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. Patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is a complex bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus. Fragments are seen. Into the intercondylar notch there is associated chondral fraying seen to the weightbearing cartilage of the medial femoral condyle as well as the tibial cartilage to a lesser degree.

There is a linear tear seen in the posterior horn and posterior body of lateral meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface with some apical truncation. There is a disruption of the lateral meniscal tibial ligament with superior displacement of the meniscal body away from the tibial plateau. No other meniscal tear is seen to the lateral meniscus. There is severe chondral thinning and fissuring and fraying seen to the weightbearing cartilage of lateral femoral condyle and to a lesser degree lateral tibial plateau.

There are no normal intact anterior cruciate ligament fibers demonstrated. There is heterogeneous thickened mixed T2 signal seen along the course of the anterior cruciate ligament. Findings are in keeping with a high-grade to complete anterior cruciate ligament tear. There is an associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst. Anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment is between 5 and 6 mm is borderline.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

The medial collateral ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst demonstrated.

There is a moderate knee effusion with mild reactive synovitis.

INTERPRETATION: 

Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus with moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment.

Complex tear of lateral meniscus involving body and posterior horn associated with what appears to be disruption of the meniscotibial attachment laterally. Severe chondrosis is seen to the lateral joint compartment.

High-grade to complete subacute to nonacute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst. Borderline anterior tibial drawer.

Moderate Baker's cyst.

Large knee effusion with synovitis.
